page: Microsoft Azure EC16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor offering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set capabilities include standard AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA extensions, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX instructions.

Hardware allocations prioritize memory capacity, providing 128.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). For fast ephemeral storage, the instance bundles 644 GB of local SSD capacity alongside support for Premium Storage. Dedicated GPU acceleration is not present on this VM shape.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier execution speeds, with single-core and multi-core evaluations placing in the middle 50% across standardized suites. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 18,629.2 and a PassMark CPU rating of 19,739.16. In memory-intensive key-value tasks, the instance recorded 15.82 million operations per second on Redis SET operations, complemented by a PassMark database score of 6,267.27.

Due to its substantial RAM-to-CPU ratio and included local SSD scratch space, the EC16ads_v5 offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise software. It is well-matched for in-memory databases, large-scale caching services, relational databases requiring fast tempdb structures, and medium-scale analytics jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure EC16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor using Microsoft Hyper-V. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory for an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The configuration integrates 644 GB of local SSD temporary storage with Premium Storage capabilities, while excluding dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark assessments position the instance consistently within the middle 50% tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 19,739.16 and reaching 15.82 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The bundled local NVMe storage and high memory footprint deliver solid cost efficiency for memory-constrained deployments, making it particularly suitable for relational database engines, Redis and Memcached nodes, large caching layers, and high-memory enterprise applications.
